item.title: Sompo Asia Pacific appoints Winnie Chau as Senior Underwriter, Financial Lines
item.description: Sompo Asia Pacific, part of global insurance and reinsurance firm Sompo, has appointed Winnie Chau as Senior Underwriter, Financial Lines, with responsibility for Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. item.title: Munafò named China CEO for Allianz Trade in Asia Pacific
item.description: Allianz Trade in Asia Pacific has announced the appointment of Scott Munafò as China CEO, a Shanghai-based role, effective September 1, 2026. Commenting on the appointment, Rodrigo Jimenez, Regional CEO at Allianz Trade in Asia Pacific, said: “Over the past decade, Scott has built extensive experience across various regions, demonstrating a strong track record in growing commercial portfolios, building strategic partnerships, and maintaining exceptional customer retention. I am confident that, together with the local management team, Scott will successfully drive our growth ambitions and deliver continued success in this important and fast-growing market.” Munafò added: “Allianz Trade has been part of China’s trade story for nearly two decades – built on the strength of our team, our partners, and our customers who have trusted us through every cycle.

item.title: Kentucky High Court Recalculates Employer Attorney Fees, Recovery in Subrogation
item.description: And an employer’s share of attorney fees must be deducted from the amount available from subrogation—not from the full settlement amount in a worker injury suit, the Kentucky Supreme Court decided in separate cases last week. The ALJ then subtracted the employer’s share of attorney fees in the suit against the vendor, leaving some $117,000 available for recovery in subrogation. Kentucky law bars injured workers from collecting duplicate benefits from the employer and a third party, and allows employers to seek recovery of benefits through subrogation.

item.title: Nuclear Verdicts Go Boom, Increase 40.7% in 2025
item.description: Verdicts like this against corporate defendants have come to be known as nuclear verdicts, and the total from 2025—a 40.7% increase over 2024—is the highest Marathon has seen since 2009. So-called “nuclear” verdicts did not subside in 2025. Product liability cases resulted in 29 nuclear verdicts totaling $12 billion in 2025.

item.title: Los Angeles Faces Days of 100F Heat as Southwest Fire Risk Grows
item.description: Los Angeles is bracing for a lengthy heat wave as the weather system that’s cooked Texas expands westward and begins stripping moisture from Southern California’s terrain. Heat alerts stretch from Santa Barbara along California’s central coast to the U.S.-Mexico border more than 200 miles (322 kilometers) southeast. Temperatures in downtown LA are forecast to approach 100F (38C) each day through Friday, according to the US National Weather Service.

item.title: NHTSA Eyeing 1 Million GM Pickups, SUVs Over Engine Failure Concerns
item.description: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Friday it has opened a probe into 997,743 General Motors pickup trucks and SUVs over concerns related to engine failure. GM issued a recall last year to address concerns related to engine failure in the impacted L87 unit. Related: Tesla Recalling 20,000 US Vehicles Over Excessively Bright Low-Beam Headlights The auto safety regulator said it received 499 complaints alleging engine failures despite the vehicles having undergone an earlier recall remedy.

item.title: Highest-Ever Ocean Temperature Measured as Super El Niño Forms
item.description: Scientists have recorded the highest temperature ever measured in the world’s oceans, as climate change combines with a powerful El Niño in the tropical Pacific. Copernicus expects the trend to continue, with ocean temperatures now being supercharged by El Niño. The August record is particularly worrying because global ocean temperatures are typically highest in March and April, after the Austral summer, Copernicus said.

item.title: Florida Example on How to Adapt as Coastal Cities Face Storms, Rising Sea Level
item.description: Recent research shows that a rise in sea level driven by humans has increased the frequency of extreme coastal flooding around the world. As climate change threatens communities, Florida is showing how to build to adapt. The goal is to better withstand rising waters, worsening storms, saltwater intrusion, heat heaves and other climate impacts.

item.title: Amazon Plans Drone Delivery Expansion to Nearly 500 U.S. Locales
item.description: Amazon said on Wednesday it will expand its drone delivery service to reach hundreds of U.S. Amazon currently delivers by drone from 11 locations, including Papillion, Nebraska, and Ruskin, Florida. Amazon said its broad rollout will extend its reach to about 500 locales.

item.title: Hurricane Lala triggers Hawaii’s parametric coral reef insurance
item.description: The Nature Conservancy’s (TNC) Hawaiʻi parametric coral reef insurance policy will pay for damage assessment and reef repairs for the first time since it purchased the United States’ first such policy four years ago, following recent impacts from Hurricane Lala which brought dangerous flooding, strong winds and major power outages across the state. Moreover, the parametric policy is designed to provide rapid funding for assessing and repairing coral reef damage caused by hurricanes and severe tropical storms across the Hawaiian Islands According to The Nature Conservancy, Hurricane Lala is the first storm—with sustained winds of 65 knots within the covered area—to trigger the insurance policy. In 2022, WTW, alongside TNC, launched the parametric coral reef insurance concept, with global reinsurer Munich Re underwriting the risk for the Hawaiian coral reef parametric insurance arrangement.

item.title: Hurricane Lala triggers The Nature Conservancy’s US coral reef insurance policy for first time
item.description: The Nature Conservancy’s (TNC) Hawaiʻi coral reef insurance policy will pay for damage assessment and reef repairs for the first time since it purchased the US’s first such policy four years ago, following Hurricane Lala’s impacts this weekend, which brought dangerous flooding, strong winds and widespread power outages across the state. This weekend’s Hurricane Lala is the first storm to trigger the insurance policy, with sustained winds of 65 knots within the covered area. Active since 2022 , the parametric policy is designed to provide rapid funding for assessing and repairing coral reef damage caused by hurricanes and severe tropical storms across the Hawaiian Islands.

Jessica brings the expertise, perspective, and leadership our clients need to manage rising severity trends, aggregation exposures, and reinsurance capacity pressures.” Ciak added: “I’m thrilled to be joining Guy Carpenter at this critical time for the medical professional liability market.

item.title: AM Best places At-Bay under review with positive implications amid Munich Re acquisition
item.description: Credit ratings agency AM Best has placed At-Bay Specialty Insurance Company (ABSIC) under review with positive implications following the recently announced acquisition of its parent company, At-Bay, Inc., by Munich Re for an enterprise value of USD 575 million. AM Best explained that the under review with positive implications status “reflects the potential financial and operational benefits that ABSIC may derive from being part of a significantly larger insurance organisation, which is of greater financial strength.” The ratings will remain under review pending completion of the transaction and AM Best’s evaluation of parental support, integration plans and the expected impact on ABSIC’s future business plans. After this, At-Bay will be overseen by Hartford Steam Boiler (HSB), part of Munich Re’s Global Specialty Insurance business.

item.title: Alfalfa Sprouts Linked to Food Poisoning in Minnesota and Wisconsin
item.description: Wisconsin investigators have identified another 18 cases of illness tied to alfalfa sprouts, Minnesota officials said. The illnesses are being linked to alfalfa sprouts produced by Everything Sprouts, a Minnesota grower, and sold under the Calco and Everything Sprouts brands to restaurants and grocery stores, Minnesota officials said. Minnesota health officials are warning consumers not to eat certain brands of alfalfa sprouts that have been tied to an unusual outbreak involving different disease-causing bacteria.

item.title: People Moves: TDI Names Kranes as Deputy Commissioner of Strategy and Performance
item.description: The Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) announced Michelle Kranes as deputy commissioner of the Strategy and Performance Division on August 17. Kranes will oversee the division that supports TDI’s strategic planning, performance and risk management, and process improvement through technology, automation, and business innovation. Kranes started her state career at the Texas Sunset Advisory Commission, where she evaluated state agencies and developed recommendations to enhance efficiency, accountability, and results.

item.title: AM Best Upgrades Credit Ratings of Arkansas’ Kinsale
item.description: AM Best has upgraded the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating (Long-Term ICR) to “a+” (Excellent) from “a” (Excellent) and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating (FSR) of A (Excellent) of Kinsale Insurance Company (Kinsale) based in Little Rock, Arkansas. These Credit Ratings (ratings) reflect Kinsale’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its strong operating performance, favorable business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM). Concurrently, AM Best has upgraded the Long-Term ICR to “bbb+” (Good) from “bbb” (Good) of Kinsale Capital Group.

item.title: Manulife launches CoverMe travel insurance app inside ChatGPT
item.description: Manulife has launched a ChatGPT app that allows Canadian travellers to receive personalised CoverMe travel insurance quotes. Once a quote is generated, they can continue to CoverMe.com, where the information provided in ChatGPT carries over to the purchase process. Users answer questions about their age, province of residence, destination, travel dates, and trip cost.

item.title: $1.6bn deal: RiverStone International takes on QBE legacy reserves
item.description: RiverStone International has entered into loss portfolio transfer reinsurance agreements with QBE Insurance, covering approximately $1.6bn of reserves. Paul Brockman, group chief executive officer of RiverStone International, welcomed the deal. The agreements expand the companies’ existing relationship and transfer responsibility for managing the legacy liabilities to RiverStone.

item.title: Branch Insurance Exchange reports Q2 2026 results
item.description: Branch Insurance Exchange, the reciprocal managed by insurance startup Branch, has released its Q2 2026 results, ending the first half with $42.2 million in written premiums, a 8.6% increase compared to the same period last year. Roughly 63% of written premium is for homeowners insurance. Net underwriting loss for the first six months was $15.3 million, ~$1 million more than the first six months of 2025.

item.title: Beyond the Screenshot: What Claims Professionals Should Expect From Digital Evidence Preservation
item.description: Federal Rule of Evidence 901 asks whether there is sufficient evidence to support a finding that an item is what its proponent claims it is. The more important question is what supporting information should be preserved so that the image can still be evaluated later. View Series Online evidence has a way of disappearing.

item.title: A Landmark Supreme Court Ruling Is Upending How America Moves Its Goods
item.description: A US Supreme Court decision in May changed the stakes for freight brokers like Ilg, opening them to lawsuits if a driver for a contracted carrier gets into a collision. Daniel Ilg started out in the freight brokerage industry at 14 years old, learning from his dad how to match trucking companies with loads of goods that needed to move around the country. The ruling leaves plenty of uncertainty about when a broker ultimately might be held responsible.

item.title: AM Best revises AmericanAg’s rating outlook to positive
item.description: AM Best has moved the outlook on American Agricultural Insurance Company’s (AmericanAg) Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating (Long-Term ICR) to positive from stable, while maintaining the company’s Financial Strength Rating (FSR) at A (Excellent) and its Long-Term ICR at “a” (Excellent), with the outlook for the FSR remaining stable. The positive outlook for the Long-Term ICR reflects what AM Best described as continued progress in AmericanAg’s operating performance. AM Best said its ratings assessment reflects AmericanAg’s strongest balance sheet strength, adequate operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).

item.title: P&C market softens further as premium decreases accelerate in Q2’26: The Council
item.description: A softening property and casualty market became clearer in the second half of 2026, as premium decreases across all account sizes accelerated to an average of 2.0% from 1.2% in the first quarter. The findings, according to The Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers’ Commercial Property/Casualty Market Report for Q2 2026, mark the second consecutive quarter of broad premium reductions across the industry. Rate relief was felt most significantly by large accounts, which experienced average premium decreases of 3.7% following a 2.7% decrease last quarter.

item.title: Clear Group acquires Lloyd’s wholesale broker NPP
item.description: Clear Group, the independent insurance intermediary, has acquired Newman Pearce & Partners LLP (NPP), a specialist Lloyd’s wholesale broker, further strengthening its presence in the London Market and accelerating its wholesale growth strategy. NPP is an independent Lloyd’s wholesale broker founded in 2019 by Gordon Newman, Neil Pearce and Colin Rogers. For Clear, this acquisition represents a significant milestone in its strategy to grow the company’s London wholesale operations.

item.title: Londoners Find ‘Horrendous’ Cracks in Their Homes After Successive Heat Waves
item.description: Londoners are facing historic levels of subsidence risk after five successive heat waves dried out the clay soil on which much of the city is built. On Reddit, people offered personal accounts telling of “ horrendous cracking ” in their homes, and “doors sticking” due to subsidence. Londoners have taken to social media to express their dismay.

item.title: KPMG Australia to Fire Hundreds of Workers as Crisis Deepens
item.description: Scandal-plagued KPMG Australia is cutting almost 400 jobs as it grapples with the fallout from allegations it misused confidential client information to win business and as demand for consulting services slows. Read more : KPMG Australia Scandal Widens After it Confirms Optus Data Was Misused “KPMG has reviewed its costs and future workforce needs in response to continued economic weakness, difficult market conditions and the impact of the firm’s conduct and whistleblower matters,” KPMG Australia said in the statement. Over the last few months, KPMG Australia has been battling the fallout from allegations it misused confidential information from companies including property developer Lendlease Group to win contracts with other corporate clients.

item.title: Former Virginia Insurance Agent Pleads Guilty to Fraud
item.description: A former Virginia insurance agent pled guilty last week to wire fraud related to a scheme to pocket the premiums he was paid for policies he sold. According to court documents, Thomas Robert Hoyt, of Melfa, told certain clients to pay premiums to him and that he would forward the payments to the insurance carriers for which he was an agent. In response to complaints, the Virginia Bureau of Insurance opened an investigation in June 2021.

item.title: Chief Specialty files trademark application
item.description: Chief Specialty Insurance Company has filed a trademark application for the name “Chief Specialty.” The August 13 filing covers insurance underwriting, including specialty insurance, as well as claims processing, claims administration, insurance administration, and the provision of specialty insurance information. The application is new and has not yet been assigned to an examiner. The applicant is based in Van Wert, Ohio.
